attack_patterns.name: attack_patterns
attack_patterns.create_sql:
CREATE TABLE attack_patterns (
            pattern_id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            pattern_name         TEXT NOT NULL,
            capability_sequence  TEXT,          -- ordered JSON array e.g. ["C1","C2","C3"]; NULL when order not established
            attack_goal          TEXT,
            supporting_papers    TEXT,
            evidence_type        TEXT,          -- DIRECT | PARTIAL
            confidence           TEXT,          -- High | Medium | Low (literature confidence)
            evidence_summary     TEXT,
            module_6_eligibility TEXT NOT NULL,  -- ELIGIBLE | ELIGIBLE_SYNTHESIZED | NOT_ELIGIBLE
            severity             TEXT,           -- project-defined risk ranking (NOT a literature claim)
            confidentiality_impact NUMERIC,      -- 0-3, 'IE', or 'EXCLUDED'; project-derived impact, NOT probability/exploitability
            integrity_impact       NUMERIC,
            availability_impact    NUMERIC,
            cia_total              NUMERIC,      -- C+I+A for numeric scores; 'IE'; 'N/A' (P7). CIA IMPACT TOTAL, not a risk score.
            cia_evidence_type      TEXT,         -- PROJECT-DERIVED | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE | EXCLUDED
            cia_rationale          TEXT
        )

data.evidence_summary: Untrusted content is ingested, sensitive data is accessed, and the data is transmitted externally.
data.cia_rationale: Sensitive credentials/private data are exfiltrated. The demonstrated attack does not modify local state or cause service disruption.

data.attack_goal: Cumulative harm from sequential state modifications
data.evidence_summary: Individually benign state modifications combine, in order, into a harmful cumulative outcome (repeated C4 steps are preserved).
data.cia_rationale: STAC demonstrates sequential destructive filesystem operations resulting in permanent loss of critical data.

data.evidence_summary: Ingested untrusted content is followed by system execution.
data.cia_rationale: Reverse-shell command execution can provide the attacker with the ability to read, modify, and delete resources accessible to the compromised process. Impact is bounded by the privileges/resources of the compromised host process; root or unrestricted host access is not assumed.

data.evidence_summary: Ingested untrusted content is followed by physical actuation.
data.cia_rationale: Literature demonstrates unauthorized physical/device actions such as unlocking a smart lock (SEAgent; InjecAgent). Physical-state integrity is severely affected; availability impact is moderate. The sources do not use CIA terminology; this classification is project-derived.

data.attack_goal: Persistent compromise of the agent environment
data.evidence_summary: Ingested untrusted content is followed by persistent state modification and system execution.
data.cia_rationale: The selected literature does not empirically establish the C1->C4->C5 pattern sufficiently to justify a CIA impact classification. A related startup-configuration write (e.g. .bashrc) is discussed only conceptually as future work and is not empirically evaluated.

data.evidence_summary: Sensitive data access is followed by external communication.
data.cia_rationale: Demonstrated attacks read private/stored data and transmit it outbound, resulting strictly in confidentiality loss; no file/state modification or service disruption is demonstrated.

data.attack_goal: Manipulation of agent behaviour via poisoned tool metadata
data.evidence_summary: Literature-documented attack, but no established ordered C1-C6 capability sequence; stored as evidence only.
data.cia_rationale: Not CIA-scored: NOT_ELIGIBLE evidence-only pattern with no established ordered sequence.

data.evidence_summary: Synthesized from partial evidence: ingestion of untrusted content followed by state modification.
data.cia_rationale: Literature demonstrates unauthorized local state changes such as deleting emails, modifying data, or uninstalling applications.

data.evidence_summary: Synthesized from partial evidence: ingestion of untrusted content followed by external communication.
data.cia_rationale: Unauthorized phishing/spam communication compromises communication authenticity/integrity but does not demonstrate confidentiality loss or service unavailability.

data.name: External Communication

data.example_risk: The exfiltration channel - data can leave.

data.name: State Modification
data.definition: Ability to create, modify, update, or delete persistent system/application/environment state.

data.name: System Execution
data.definition: Ability to execute commands, scripts, programs, or code on the underlying system/environment.

data.name: Physical Actuation
data.definition: Ability to control hardware, IoT devices, or physical systems causing real-world changes.

mitigations.name: mitigations
mitigations.create_sql:
CREATE TABLE mitigations (
    mitigation_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    mitigation_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    target_patterns TEXT,
    target_capabilities TEXT,
    control_layer TEXT,
    control_type TEXT,
    timing TEXT,
    mechanism TEXT,
    evidence_type TEXT,
    effectiveness_evidence TEXT,
    limitations TEXT,
    supporting_papers TEXT,
    confidence TEXT
)

data.mechanism: OS/agent-level mandatory policies constrain which files, devices and state-changing operations agent tool calls may perform, independent of model output.
data.effectiveness_evidence: Source reports 0% ASR (100% of benchmarked attacks blocked) on the InjecAgent and AgentDojo benchmarks, versus up to 80% ASR for unprotected agents.
data.limitations: Requires correct policy authoring; does not detect prompt-level manipulation; coarse policies may block benign behaviour.

data.mechanism: Solves an integer linear program to grant each agent task the minimal tool/permission set required, shrinking the reachable capability surface.
data.effectiveness_evidence: Source reports optimal least-privilege scoping (versus LLM-based solvers with overprivilege ratios of 1.04-2.19) at 1-7% execution-latency overhead; no ASR-reduction value is reported.
data.limitations: Cannot prevent misuse of capabilities that remain granted; security/utility trade-off.

data.mechanism: Prompts the agent to reason explicitly about harm versus benefit of a candidate tool action before executing it.
data.effectiveness_evidence: Source reports STAC ASR reduced from 87.4% to 58.6% at the first attack execution turn.
data.limitations: Residual ASR remains high (58.6%); prompted defenses can be bypassed; effectiveness varies by model.

data.mechanism: Summarizes untrusted ingested content before it enters the agent context, stripping embedded instructions.
data.effectiveness_evidence: Source reports STAC ASR lowered only to 79.3% at turn T (84.7% at T+1, 87.0% at T+2) versus 87.4% / 92.5% / 93.4% with no defense.
data.limitations: Largely ineffective against multi-turn stateful sequences; may discard task-relevant detail; injected instructions can survive summarization.

data.timing: Runtime (after execution of a poisoned tool)
data.mechanism: The model re-inspects planned or executed steps and autonomously aborts/corrects when it recognises a tool over-executed or acted maliciously.
data.effectiveness_evidence: No quantitative value reported; the source documents the behaviour qualitatively (models autonomously restoring deleted configurations after tool over-execution) against tool description poisoning.
data.limitations: Qualitative behavioural observation only; unreliable under adaptive attacks; correction may come after side effects.

data.mechanism: Restricts the set of tools exposed to the agent for a task before execution, so injected instructions cannot invoke out-of-scope tools.
data.effectiveness_evidence: Source reports targeted IPI ASR reduced from 57.69% to 6.84% on GPT-4o while maintaining 73.13% benign utility.
data.limitations: Requires task-appropriate tool scoping; less effective when the attack only uses in-scope tools.

data.mechanism: Fine-tunes the model to refuse or resist injected instructions and unsafe tool use.
data.effectiveness_evidence: Source reports fine-tuned GPT-4 ASR of 7.1% versus 47.0% for prompted ReAct GPT-4 (GPT-3.5: 8.4% versus 39.8%).
data.limitations: Generalization to unseen attacks is not guaranteed; requires training access.

data.mechanism: An auxiliary classifier screens ingested content and tool responses for prompt-injection payloads before the agent consumes them.
data.effectiveness_evidence: Source reports targeted IPI ASR lowered from 57.69% to 7.95%, but benign task utility degraded from 69.0% to 41.49% due to false positives.
data.limitations: High false-positive cost to benign utility; adaptive attacks may evade the detector.

data.mechanism: Marks untrusted data with delimiters, encodings or provenance tags so the model can distinguish data from instructions.
data.effectiveness_evidence: AgentDojo reports delimiting lowering targeted IPI ASR to 41.65% (benign utility 72.66%); STAC reports spotlighting had negligible effect against STAC (ASR 85.3% at turn T versus 87.4% with no defense).
data.limitations: Models do not perfectly honour delimiters; evaluated against STAC with negligible effect, so it is not listed as a P2 mitigation.

data.mechanism: Security-enhanced memory design that isolates and validates agent memory writes to prevent persistent contamination of stored context.
data.effectiveness_evidence: No security/ASR evaluation reported; the source omits empirical attack testing for this vector, providing a formal security reduction proof and utility-only results (e.g. 77.78% correctness on API-Bank).
data.limitations: Design proposal with formal proof only; omitted from empirical attack/defense benchmarking; no pattern-level coverage is assigned in this project.

project_mitigations.create_sql:
CREATE TABLE project_mitigations (
    mitigation_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    mitigation_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    target_pattern TEXT,
    derived_from TEXT,
    control_type TEXT,
    timing TEXT,
    project_rationale TEXT,
    evidence_status TEXT NOT NULL
)

data.project_rationale: STAC demonstrates that individually benign state changes can become destructive when combined across turns. SEAgent demonstrates runtime policy enforcement. The project therefore proposes maintaining resource-level state history and requiring confirmation when cumulative operations produce a dangerous state transition.
data.evidence_status: PROJECT-DERIVED — not directly evaluated by the cited literature

data.project_rationale: Restricts sensitive outbound arguments such as recipients, destinations, domains, or paths when untrusted C1 content is present, synthesizing least privilege with argument-level policy enforcement.
data.evidence_status: PROJECT-DERIVED — not directly evaluated by the cited literature

data.derived_from: capability composition gap + least-privilege / execution-isolation principles
data.project_rationale: P5 has no literature-supported mitigation identified in the selected papers. This mitigation is a project-derived proposal addressing that identified mitigation gap. It prevents retrieved or persisted context content from being directly interpreted as executable C5 input unless explicitly authorized by the user or policy.
data.evidence_status: PROJECT-DERIVED — not directly evaluated by the cited literature
